Interface InPlaceResourceReloader

All Superinterfaces:
Ordered
public interface InPlaceResourceReloader extends Ordered
Applies a change of the application's resources to the running application in place, so that a development launcher need not restart it.

A launcher that found resources changed in its reloadable roots, and no class, asks the reloaders of the running context, in order, before it restarts: the first that can take the whole change applies it. The launcher makes the new contents readable through the context's class loader first, so that a reloader reads them as it would after a restart. A reloader that throws refuses the change, and the launcher restarts instead: the new generation it builds discards whatever the reloader had applied before it failed, which is why a reloader need not undo a partial change.

Implementations are beans that exist only while development mode is active (@DevelopmentActive). The Python runtime's reloader patches the changed modules into every running interpreter, keeping their module, class and function objects, which the generated classes and the caches built on them still refer to.

Resources are named by their path relative to the root of the class path that holds them, with / as separator, as ClassLoader.getResource(String) names them.

  • Method Details

    • canReload

      boolean canReload(Set<String> changedResources, Set<String> removedResources)
      Whether this reloader can apply the whole change in place. Called before the new contents are readable, so the answer depends on the names alone. A reloader answers false for a change that holds a resource it does not handle, or one it cannot apply, such as one that adds or removes a resource.
      Parameters:
      changedResources - The resources whose contents changed
      removedResources - The resources removed
      Returns:
      True if reload(Set) would apply every one of them

    • reload

      InPlaceResourceReloader.Result reload(Set<String> changedResources) throws Exception
      Applies the change to the running application. The new contents are readable through the application context's class loader when this is called.
      Parameters:
      changedResources - The resources whose contents changed
      Returns:
      What was reloaded, for the launcher to report
      Throws:
      Exception - to refuse the change, after which the launcher restarts the application
